title: Serialize settings override writes through one revision-aware store
description:
Problem: independent settings services can load the same override document, mutate stale copies, and overwrite each other using a shared temporary-file pattern. Concurrent updates can lose unrelated changes or collide during replacement.

Desired outcome: all settings override mutations use one process-wide store that serializes read-modify-write operations and detects stale revisions.

Scope:
- Introduce a shared settings override store for all mutation paths.
- Use an async write lock and unique temporary file names per operation.
- Add revision or compare-and-swap checks for stale writers.
- Preserve atomic replacement and clear failure diagnostics.
- Out of scope: replacing the configuration format.

Acceptance criteria:
- Concurrent updates to disjoint settings paths preserve both changes.
- Stale revisions fail or retry according to an explicit policy rather than silently overwriting newer data.
- Temporary files cannot collide between concurrent writers.
- Failed writes preserve the last valid document.
- Focused concurrency and recovery tests cover administrator and model-profile mutations.

Validation:
- Run focused configuration/settings tests with concurrent writers.
- Run the application build.
- Run Test-TaskRecords.ps1 after task metadata changes.
